summary: The most probable root cause is the order-router-00418 deploy ("refactor order validation") at 13:09 UTC. The order-router error rate stepped from about 0.004 to 0.155 in the 13:10 bucket and to about 0.305 by 13:11, and the first ERROR was logged at 13:10:07Z. Every ERROR line reviewed in the window is the same unhandled KeyError 'limit_price' in place_order, and downstream services (broker-gateway, orchestrator, postgres, redis, rabbitmq) look healthy. The failure was still occurring near 14:00. The direct code link is unverified because no diff was available, so the mechanism (limit_price read unconditionally, likely hitting a subset of order types) is an assumption. Rolling back order-router-00418 is the indicated immediate action, consistent with the earlier INC-0431.

hypotheses.statement: The order-router-00418 deploy (refactor order validation) introduced a regression so that place_order reads 'limit_price' unconditionally and raises an unhandled KeyError on requests without it, failing about 30% of order placements from 13:10 while downstream services stay healthy.
hypotheses.label: high

supporting.text: order-router-00418 ("refactor order validation") was deployed at 13:09 UTC, about one minute before the reported onset, and it is the only change for order-router in the 12:00-14:00 window (no config, migration or flag changes).
order-router err_rate was flat and low (0.003-0.006) until 13:09, then rose to 0.155 in the 13:10 bucket and plateaued near 0.30, a step change aligned with the deploy.

The first ERROR is at 13:10:07Z, an unhandled KeyError 'limit_price' in place_order. All 96 errors in 13:10-13:26 and all 60 errors in 13:00-13:20 are this same message, and every shown line in the later window is too, with the last at 13:59:33, so the failure was still occurring near the end of the window.
Downstream broker-gateway and orchestrator error rates stayed low, so the failure is localised to order-router rather than coming from a downstream dependency.
Traffic stayed flat, so the errors are not explained by a load change.
A past incident (INC-0431) had the same pattern: a validation regression in an order-router release, fixed by rollback. This is only a hint, not proof for the current incident.

It is likely that the refactor changed validation so that limit_price is read for all order types, which would explain the KeyError and the partial (about 30%) failure rate. This is an assumption: the diff has not been checked, and the logs do not show which order types fail.

contradicting.text: The link between the refactor and the KeyError rests on timing and log content. No code diff is available, and the change record does not say which validation logic changed.

Logs and metrics do not reconcile on error volume. An err_rate near 0.30 at about 20 rps implies roughly 6 failures per second, but only about 6 ERROR lines per minute appear. The logs may be sampled or err_rate may count something else, so the log volume cannot fully account for the metric.

It is not shown which order types or users fail. The search for 'market' returned nothing, but the error text has no order-type field, so it proves nothing. The assumption that only some order types are affected is unverified.
Log coverage of the later window is incomplete: 204 matches with truncation, so the message mix in the unseen tail is unverified.
